points.reached by: The bus_req_i ==> tx_fifo.wdata arrow carries bus_req_i.data into this logic block.
points.reason: The bus write data is concatenated into the FIFO word, so changing the input can change the transmitted payload.

points.reached by: The tx_fifo.wdata ==> data_buffer arrow carries tx_fifo.wdata into the FIFO instance.
points.reason: The another-IP FIFO stores the written payload and returns it as rdata, so an altered FIFO write can alter the later payload.

points.reached by: The data_buffer ==> serial_engine arrow carries tx_fifo.rdata into the serial engine.
points.reason: The engine loads and shifts the FIFO word in serial.sreg and directly drives the externally observable neooled_o waveform.

points.reached by: The serial_engine ==> serial.next_bit arrow carries a selected bit of serial.sreg into this logic block.
points.reason: This internal bit is only a forwarding value used to select timing and is not itself exposed or independently writable at this point.

points.reached by: The bus_req_i ==> bus_access arrow carries the control-write data and access conditions into the holding process.
points.reason: A bus write changes ctrl.enable, which directly drives clkgen_en_o, clears the FIFO when disabled, and controls serial engine state.

points.reached by: The bus_access ==> tx_fifo.clear arrow carries the inverted ctrl.enable decision into this logic block.
points.reason: This block only forwards the enable-derived clear control to the FIFO; it does not store or expose the enable state itself.

points.reached by: The tx_fifo.clear ==> data_buffer arrow carries the clear control into the FIFO instance.
points.reason: The FIFO clear input affects queued payload data rather than modifying or exposing the enable state.

points.reached by: The bus_access ==> serial_engine arrow carries ctrl.enable into the serial engine.
points.reason: The enable controls the engine state and disabling it causes the normal serial operation to remain inactive.

points.reached by: The bus_access ==> irq_generator arrow carries ctrl.enable into the interrupt calculation.
points.reason: The interrupt calculation observes enable but does not store, expose, or change the enable state.

points.reached by: The bus_access ==> clkgen_en_o arrow reaches the concurrent assignment driving this output.
points.reason: The output is an unmixed copy of ctrl.enable, so changing or blocking it changes whether external clock generation is enabled.

points.reached by: The bus_req_i ==> bus_access arrow carries the mode and strobe write data and access conditions into the holding process.
points.reason: Bus writes directly replace ctrl.mode and ctrl.strobe, which are the settings selecting the transmission format.

points.reached by: The bus_access ==> tx_fifo.wdata arrow carries ctrl.mode and ctrl.strobe into the FIFO write word.
points.reason: The format controls are inserted into each queued word and can therefore affect how that word is interpreted.

points.reached by: The tx_fifo.wdata ==> data_buffer arrow carries the format-tagged word into the FIFO instance.
points.reason: The FIFO stores the mode and strobe tags together with the payload that the serial engine later interprets.

points.reached by: The data_buffer ==> serial_engine arrow carries tx_fifo.rdata, including its mode and strobe bits, into the engine.
points.reason: The queued mode and strobe bits select serial.mode, bit count, and the subsequent engine state, changing the protocol sequence.

points.reached by: The bus_req_i ==> bus_access arrow carries the timing-configuration write data and access conditions into the holding process.
points.reason: Bus writes directly replace the prescaler and timing-limit registers, so an attacker can program invalid or non-progressing timing.

points.reached by: The bus_access ==> serial_engine arrow carries ctrl.clk_prsc and the timing values into the serial engine.
points.reason: The configuration selects the sampled clock and pulse limits, and unsuitable values can corrupt the waveform or prevent the state machine from completing.

points.reached by: The held irq_o assignment is in irq_generator, which combines enable, irq_conf, and FIFO status.
points.reason: The process computes irq_o from control and FIFO-status conditions, so those conditions can make the interrupt assertion incorrect.

points.reached by: The data_buffer ==> irq_generator arrow carries tx_fifo.avail and tx_fifo.half into the interrupt calculation.
points.reason: The FIFO instance produces the availability and half-full flags that determine the interrupt condition.

points.reached by: The tx_fifo.we ==> data_buffer arrow reaches the FIFO source of the interrupt status.
points.reason: The write strobe changes FIFO occupancy and therefore can change the flags used to generate irq_o.

points.reached by: The tx_fifo.re ==> data_buffer arrow reaches the FIFO source of the interrupt status.
points.reason: The serial-engine-driven read strobe changes FIFO occupancy and can alter the availability and half-full flags.

points.reached by: The tx_fifo.clear ==> data_buffer arrow reaches the FIFO clear input that affects its status.
points.reason: The clear control can reset FIFO occupancy and thereby change the status used for irq_o.

points.reached by: The data_buffer and bus_access blocks both feed the irq_generator point; bus_access supplies ctrl.enable and ctrl.irq_conf.
points.reason: Unchecked writes can alter the enable and interrupt-threshold selection used to compute irq_o.

points.reached by: The serial_engine --> tx_fifo.re arrow makes the serial engine an influence point for the FIFO status feeding irq_generator.
points.reason: The engine state determines when the FIFO is read, which changes the occupancy flags on which irq_o depends.
